clue.text: Aggressive pitch (not the padded sort, it's said?)

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase the bracket describes is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a prison room with bare walls, unlike the padded room of an asylum

explanation.surface: A sales pitch so forceful it's compared to an unpadded room.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket describes a HARD CELL (one without padding); said aloud it gives the high-pressure sales technique.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressive sales pitch is the pushy, high-pressure selling style known by this phrase.

clue.text: Brass slate often seen on the range

parts.note: brass is cheek or impudence, informally sauce
to slate is to criticise harshly, informally to pan

explanation.surface: A brass plaque or slate tile commonly found on a kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' and 'slate' look like materials, but they are cheek and criticise; a range here is a kitchen cooking stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking pot with a handle is a familiar sight on a kitchen stove or range.

clue.text: See 1
Musical composition, if a satnav turned volume off

indicators.note: turned tells us the letters of the fodder are spun into a new order
off tells us the volume letter is taken away from the device name

explanation.surface: A piece of music made if a GPS device had its sound muted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes V from SATNAV, and 'turned' rearranges IFASATNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasia is a free-form musical piece, one following the composer's imagination rather than a set structure.

clue.text: Blair originally: "Zero tolerance at the heart, I say"

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: at the heart picks the central letter of the word tolerance

parts.note: well and I say are both mild exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A quotation from Tony Blair's early days about a zero-tolerance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blair is not Tony but Eric Blair, whose original name was replaced by his famous pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Arthur Blair was the birth name of the author of Animal Farm, so the pen name is what Blair originally became.

clue.text: Guardian supporting Shakespearean character faring well

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in The Tempest
the setter writes for the Guardian, so the paper can call itself us

explanation.surface: A newspaper backing a Shakespeare figure who is doing nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' places US below PROSPERO; Guardian setters often use the paper to mean US.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone faring well is thriving and successful, which is what being wealthy and flourishing means.

clue.text: See 26
Old sporting hero Coe over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the name is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Seb Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: Sebastian Coe, a former athletics star, past his prime.
explanation.walkthrough: Coe looks like the hero, but only his first name is used; the hero is George Best, the Manchester United and Northern Ireland footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best was a celebrated footballer of the 1960s and 70s, a sporting hero of the past.

clue.text: In which Sydney features prominently (though neither of those alluded to)

definitions.text: In which Sydney features prominently (though neither of those alluded to)

parts.words: In which Sydney features prominently (though neither of those alluded to)
parts.note: Sydney Carton is the hero of the Dickens novel, and the bracket warns that neither Sydney, Australia, nor Sydney, Nova Scotia, is meant

explanation.surface: A book prominently featuring Sydney, though not the place you'd think.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney suggests the Australian city; it is Sydney Carton, who goes to the guillotine in Dickens's novel of London and Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens novel set in London and Paris has Sydney Carton as a central figure.

clue.text: Carrier's fan carrier almost capsized

indicators.note: capsized means turned over, so the letters are upset into a new order
almost means the last letter of the second word is dropped

explanation.surface: A boat carrying a fan nearly overturns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CARRIER to CARRIE; 'capsized' rearranges FANCARRIE. The 's is 'is', the clue's link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national airline is an air carrier.

clue.text: Month one: gets quaintly drunk on approx. a sixth of a pint

definitions.text: approx. a sixth of a pint

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
I is the Roman numeral for one
lit is a dated, quaint word for intoxicated
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: In the first month someone gets old-fashionedly tipsy on a small measure of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of a litre is 100 millilitres, roughly 0.18 of an imperial pint.

clue.text: Tobacco in can — lots rejected (contains uranium)

indicators.note: contains signals that the reversed word wraps around the chemical symbol
rejected means sent back, so the word for lots is read backwards

parts.note: tons is informal for lots
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A tin of tobacco, much of it thrown out because it holds radioactive material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for prison, where tobacco is called snout.
explanation.definitionFit: In British prison slang snout means tobacco or a cigarette, and can is slang for jail.

clue.text: See 26 down
Went furtively topless but did nothing?

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to sidle is to move in a stealthy, furtive way

explanation.surface: Someone sneaked about half-naked but achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests nudity; it drops the S from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To have idled is to have been lazy, to have done nothing useful.

clue.text: Devious clue: "Following from French uprising: German chap wearing girdle"

indicators.note: wearing means the girdle is put on around the following pieces

parts.note: a ring encircles, just as a girdle does

indicators.note: Following means the German chap comes after the French piece
uprising in a down clue means the French word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: de is French for from
Herr is German for Mr, a German man

explanation.surface: A tricky crossword clue describing a French revolt and a belted German man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses the French word, as down entries read upwards; 'Following' puts the German chap after it, and 'wearing' places both inside the girdle.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue that deliberately throws people off the scent.

clue.text: Shakespeare character's earliest manifestation lacks independence

indicators.note: manifestation suggests a fresh form being shown, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacks means one letter is missing from the word earliest

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independence, or Independent

explanation.surface: The first appearance of a Shakespeare figure shows he is not free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes I from EARLIEST, and 'manifestation' rearranges EARLEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is Ophelia's brother in Hamlet, who duels with the prince.

clue.text: Rock scorer's "Stumped" single

parts.note: on a cricket scorecard st is the abbreviation for stumped
single means one

explanation.surface: A rock musician's stage name and a single.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is stumped when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batsman is out of the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone is a piece of rock.

clue.text: Score on date, with internal covering

parts.note: to score is to mark with a line

explanation.surface: Marking a date with a scratch, plus padding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lined has a layer such as fabric covering its inside surface.

clue.text: Period hack, good for Times

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: to hack is to chop, as with an axe
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A journalist of the day, a fine writer for The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' suggests a journalist and Times the newspaper; G replaces the multiplication sign X in AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a period of time or historical era.

clue.text: No longer number one comprehending depth computer technology? Speed up!

parts.note: ex means former, no longer

indicators.note: comprehending means including, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for urination
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A former top boss, after grasping deep computing, urges faster work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' suggests the leader, but it is the nursery euphemism for urinating; 'comprehending' puts depth and computer technology inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite something is to make it happen more quickly.

clue.text: See 9
Cross piece over entrance to cellar?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole combined run is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix or cross
a part is a piece

explanation.surface: A crucifix piece placed above a door into the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ROODPART as a whole; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged hatch in the floor is a common way down into a cellar.

clue.text: Devil responsible for 9 20 23

definitions.meaning: the ... is an old euphemism for the devil, as in what the ...
Charles ... wrote the novel at 9 across

explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens wrote the novel, and the dickens is a mild euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: See 9
Unkempt as a cormorant?

definitions.meaning: a shag is a cormorant-like seabird, so jokingly this is like a shag

explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy means rough and untidy, and the shag is a type of cormorant, so shag-like.

clue.text: Frank might show it's paid, getting job to get on

parts.note: a post is a job or position
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: Someone frank shows he's been paid, landing a job to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: A frank is a postal mark showing the postage has been paid; Frank is not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A franking mark on an envelope shows that the cost of sending it has been paid.

clue.text: Carbon-14 measurer, say, who's arranged a partner?

definitions.meaning: something that dates, like a radiocarbon test
someone who goes on dates with a partner

explanation.definitionFit: A dater is something that fixes a date, as radiocarbon dating does, or a person dating someone.

clue.text: 9 20 23 by 5, comprehensively losing a couple of capital boxing bouts?

definitions.text: comprehensively losing a couple of capital boxing bouts?
definitions.meaning: a boxer comprehensively beaten in a bout in each of two capitals

explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's memoir of poverty in two capitals is a tale of two cities; read literally it is a boxer floored in both.

clue.text: See 26 down
City's permission to seize document

indicators.note: to seize means the first piece grabs and holds the second inside it

parts.note: OK is permission, as in giving the OK
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a document

explanation.surface: A city's authorisation to confiscate paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in Siberia, Russia.

clue.text: Succeeding when planting kiss in lacy material

indicators.note: planting means placing one piece within another
in shows where the kiss is placed, inside the material

parts.note: net is a lacy fabric
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Success when a kiss is placed into delicate lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means following on, coming after in sequence.

clue.text: Overheard description of Don Quixote's end of a working day?

indicators.note: overheard means the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Cervantes's hero is a feeble, ineffectual knight errant, a weak knight

explanation.surface: A description of Cervantes's hero overheard at the end of a working day.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Quixote is the deluded, frail would-be knight in Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening on a working day, Monday to Friday, comes at the end of that working day.

clue.text: Anxious about unarticled Native Americans

indicators.note: about signals that the remaining letters are moved around
unarticled means the indefinite article is taken out of the word

explanation.surface: Worried about Native Americans who have no articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unarticled' removes the article AN from ANXIOUS, and 'about' rearranges XIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are a group of Native American peoples of the Great Plains.
